title: ELECTION GUIDE: Antonia 'Toni' Arteaga Q&A - NewsBreak
text:
5 hours ago Antonia "Toni" Arteaga (Courtesy/Antonia "Toni" Arteaga) Name: Antonia “Toni” Arteaga
Age: 55
Education: The University of Texas at Austin (Bachelors Degree)
St. Mary’s University School of Law (J.D.)
Previous elected office: Currently serving my 5th term as Judge of the 57th District Court
1. Why are you the best qualified candidate to take on this position?
I am uniquely qualified to serve as your next Chief Justice of the 4th Court of Appeals for a number of reasons, including:
I am the only candidate with almost 20 years of consecutive judicial experience. I am the only candidate that has served in courts that handle criminal and civil law. I am the only candidate with more than a decade of extensive executive experience on a local, state and national level. I am the only candidate elected twice by judges from across the state to advocate legislatively for all issues that effect the judiciary. Growing up as the youngest of eight daughters in a small community with humble beginnings has given me a unique perspective on how the law affects individuals and families in their daily lives. Elected in 2008, I am the longest serving judge at the Bexar County Courthouse and am currently serving in my 5th term.
The Fourth Court handles both civil and criminal appeals. Thus, it is very important that I am the only candidate that has served in courts that handle criminal and civil law.
As an attorney, I tried to verdict over 70 criminal jury trials. Additionally, I was twice appointed by former Chief Justice, then-mayor Phil Hardberger, to serve as a Criminal Law Magistrate.
In 2008, I became the first woman elected as Judge of the 57th District Court - where I continue to preside over the most complex and difficult civil law cases and long civil jury trials.
The Chief Justice is also the administrative head and chief executive officer of the Court. I am the only candidate with extensive executive experience on the local, state and national level.
Locally, as Bexar County’s Court Security Chair, I organized and implemented the first Active Shooter Training for the entire courthouse complex. As President of the Texas Association for District Judges, I lead the legislatively efforts for our members which consisted of over 400 judges from all over the state. Currently, I also serve as President of the Texas Latinx Judges which I co-founded almost five years ago. Nationally, I have served as the local Chair for the National Campaign to Stop Violence for more than ten years.
Finally, I bring to the court a unique perspective. Growing up as the youngest of eight daughters in a small community with humble beginnings has given me a unique perspective on how the law affects individuals and families in their daily lives. Furthermore, voting for me, Antonia “Toni” Arteaga, ensures we keep three Democrats on the 4th Court of Appeals, and we keep the position of Chief Justice in the most qualified hands and in hands that you trust.
2. How does Webb County’s location as a border community affect the types of cases that come before your court, and how should the judiciary respond to those challenges while remaining impartial?
Webb County’s location on the border means cases may involve jurisdictional issues and be more apt to have heightened media attention.
The Court’s responsibility in border communities is the same as everywhere else – cases must be decided based on the record, the briefs and the law.
My family has ties to Laredo, and my husband’s family is from Laredo, which only deepens my appreciation for Webb County.
3. What is one issue specific to your district you plan to address if elected?
One issue affecting this large district, including Webb County, is the need for timely and clear appellate decisions. Communities deserve rulings that are consistent and issued without unnecessary delay.
As Chief Justice, I will focus on efficient case administration and opinions that provide clear practical guidance to trial courts and litigants. Drawing on my real-world experience administering busy trial courts, I understand how appellate clarity directly affects day-to-day operations. Communicating the law clearly helps resolve cases more efficiently, costs are reduced, and confidence in the justice system is strengthened.
4. What principles would guide your decisions from the bench?
My decisions are guided by the law. Judges must apply the law as written and ensure that each person who appears before the court knows their case was heard and feel that they had their opportunity to have their day in court.---
5. How do you ensure consistency in sentencing or rulings?
Consistency begins with preparation and adherence to the law.
At the appellate level, trial judges appreciate a careful legal analysis, clear written opinions that explain the reasoning behind a decision and opinions that are delivered professionally and are respectful of the trial judge’s perspective.
6. Have you ever been arrested or convicted of any crime? If so, explain the circumstances and the outcome.
Never.
